account: Today appears outwardly routine, but several details suggest neighbours may be arranging something together without telling me. Townsfolk reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and a sack of bread at the inn; I also saw the baker replenish the market stall. Bread at the inn could simply be normal trade. More unusually, the innkeeper requested tomorrow at 18:00 in the great hall and specifically asked that I not arrive early. I approved that appointment. My neighbour now says they met the innkeeper, builder, freight, baker, and my secretary this morning, and offered help with baking. They describe people readily helping one another, but have not said what the help was for. A lantern was installed in the town hall this morning, though I do not know by whom or why. Taken together, a shared meal or surprise gathering tomorrow seems plausible, possibly involving baking, supplies, and preparations in the hall. I do not have proof that these events are connected, nor that anything improper is happening. The secretary confirmed my tea here, and the neighbour has been friendly but general about the morning's activities. I should keep my appointments, return to the office for 16:30, and learn more through ordinary conversation rather than treat speculation as fact.
